text:
Record the Jarvis Python→Node.js rewrite: The original Jarvis at ~/Jarvis2/ was a Python-based AI assistant with PyQt6 desktop UI, voice interaction (SpeechRecognition + pyttsx3/edge-tts), and SQLite memory. It had 60+ Python files across core, voice, ui, skills, and tools modules.

The rewrite created an equivalent Node.js/TypeScript project at ~/Desktop/Jarvis 55/ with 13 TypeScript source files. Key conversions: engine.py→src/core/engine.ts, llm_engine.py→src/core/llmEngine.ts (using OpenAI SDK against Ollama), memory.py→src/core/memory.ts (better-sqlite3), emotion.py→src/core/emotion.ts (lexicon-based Plutchik), speaker.py→src/voice/speaker.ts (MsEdgeTTS), listener.py→src/voice/listener.ts (node-microphone). Added wakeWord.ts for wake word detection. The project uses npm workspaces, tsx for TypeScript execution, and the visual-ai-architect subproject provides the web UI.
title: Auto-learned conversation

text:
Record the Jarvis 55 frontend integration: A JarvisDashboard React component was created inside the VACA frontend at components/jarvis/JarvisDashboard.tsx with chat interface, system status sidebar, and placeholder widgets. A "🤖 Jarvis" toggle button was added to App.tsx header with conditional rendering to switch between VACA canvas mode and Jarvis assistant mode.

The integration involved: (1) Creating components/jarvis/JarvisDashboard.tsx with full chat UI, sidebar (system status, skills, commands), message history with typing indicator, and input area. (2) Creating matching CSS using VACA theme variables. (3) Modifying App.tsx to add import, jarvisMode state, header toggle button (purple #7c3aed theme), and conditional rendering: when jarvisMode is true, JarvisDashboard renders instead of the normal VACA canvas. Back button returns to canvas. The chat uses /api/reason endpoint for LLM responses and /api/config/llm + /health for system status polling.
title: Auto-learned conversation

text:
Record the Jarvis 55 npm scripts and entry points: The rewritten project has these npm scripts - start: tsx src/index.ts (voice-first default mode with wake word detection), start:cli: tsx src/index.ts --cli (interactive terminal chat), start:desktop: tsx src/index.ts --backend (headless IPC socket at /tmp/jarvis.sock), dev: tsx watch src/index.ts --cli (CLI with autoreload), dev:web: concurrently starts Vite frontend on :5173, VACA backend on :3001, and Jarvis backend mode with IPC. Train: tsx src/index.ts --train shows memory stats. Models: tsx src/index.ts --models lists Ollama models. Export: tsx src/index.ts --export saves datasheets. Rules: tsx src/index.ts --rules shows active rules.

The CLI entry point (src/index.ts) supports: --cli mode with /help, /models, /stats, /remind, /export, /exit commands. --backend mode creates a Unix socket server at /tmp/jarvis.sock that accepts JSON-line commands: {"action":"chat","message":"..."} and {"action":"ping"}. Default voice mode uses WakeWordDetector, Speaker, and Listener modules. All modes have graceful SIGINT shutdown that calls engine.shutdown() to close SQLite and stop the scheduler.
title: Auto-learned conversation

text:
Record the Jarvis 2→55 copy and setup process: The entire Jarvis2 project (15GB) at ~/Desktop/Jarvis2/ was copied to ~/Desktop/Jarvis 55/ using rsync, excluding node_modules, .git, dist, and __pycache__. Fresh npm install added 164 packages. Shell scripts (start-jarvis.sh, start-desktop.sh, start-jarvis2.sh) were updated to use npx tsx instead of Python. A .gitignore was created for node_modules, dist, .db, .env, and logs. The config.yaml was kept and is now read by the TypeScript config loader via js-yaml.

The copy was executed with: rsync -av --exclude=node_modules --exclude=.git --exclude=dist --exclude=__pycache__ --exclude=.pytest_cache /home/final-flash1/Desktop/Jarvis2/ "/home/final-flash1/Desktop/Jarvis 55/". 13.9GB transferred at ~489MB/s. npm install completed in 4 seconds adding 164 packages. TypeScript typecheck passes with 0 errors. The project has 13 source files, a full VACA subproject with React frontend, and GGUF models (7.3GB). npm scripts available: start (voice-first), start:cli, start:desktop (--backend IPC), dev (CLI autoreload), dev:web (full VACA stack), train, models, export, rules.
title: Auto-learned conversation
